nodes.Name: UintSize
nodes.DocComment: UintSize is the size of a uint in bits.

nodes.Name: LeadingZeros
nodes.DocComment: LeadingZeros returns the number of leading zero bits in x; the result is [UintSize] for x == 0.

nodes.Name: RotateLeft
nodes.DocComment:
RotateLeft returns the value of x rotated left by (k mod [UintSize]) bits.
To rotate x right by k bits, call RotateLeft(x, -k).

This function's execution time does not depend on the inputs.

nodes.Name: Add
nodes.DocComment:
Add returns the sum with carry of x, y and carry: sum = x + y + carry.
The carry input must be 0 or 1; otherwise the behavior is undefined.
The carryOut output is guaranteed to be 0 or 1.

This function's execution time does not depend on the inputs.

nodes.Name: Add32
nodes.DocComment:
Add32 returns the sum with carry of x, y and carry: sum = x + y + carry.
The carry input must be 0 or 1; otherwise the behavior is undefined.
The carryOut output is guaranteed to be 0 or 1.

This function's execution time does not depend on the inputs.

nodes.Name: Add64
nodes.DocComment:

The carry input must be 0 or 1; otherwise the behavior is undefined.
The carryOut output is guaranteed to be 0 or 1.

This function's execution time does not depend on the inputs.

nodes.Name: Sub
nodes.DocComment:
Sub returns the difference of x, y and borrow: diff = x - y - borrow.
The borrow input must be 0 or 1; otherwise the behavior is undefined.
The borrowOut output is guaranteed to be 0 or 1.

This function's execution time does not depend on the inputs.

nodes.Name: Sub32
nodes.DocComment:
Sub32 returns the difference of x, y and borrow, diff = x - y - borrow.
The borrow input must be 0 or 1; otherwise the behavior is undefined.
The borrowOut output is guaranteed to be 0 or 1.

This function's execution time does not depend on the inputs.

The borrow input must be 0 or 1; otherwise the behavior is undefined.
The borrowOut output is guaranteed to be 0 or 1.

This function's execution time does not depend on the inputs.

nodes.Name: Mul
nodes.DocComment:
Mul returns the full-width product of x and y: (hi, lo) = x * y
with the product bits' upper half returned in hi and the lower
half returned in lo.

This function's execution time does not depend on the inputs.

nodes.Name: Mul32
nodes.DocComment:
Mul32 returns the 64-bit product of x and y: (hi, lo) = x * y
with the product bits' upper half returned in hi and the lower
half returned in lo.

This function's execution time does not depend on the inputs.

nodes.Name: Mul64
nodes.DocComment:
Mul64 returns the 128-bit product of x and y: (hi, lo) = x * y
with the product bits' upper half returned in hi and the lower
half returned in lo.

This function's execution time does not depend on the inputs.

nodes.Name: Div
nodes.DocComment:
Div returns the quotient and remainder of (hi, lo) divided by y:
quo = (hi, lo)/y, rem = (hi, lo)%y with the dividend bits' upper
half in parameter hi and the lower half in parameter lo.
Div panics for y == 0 (division by zero) or y <= hi (quotient overflow).

nodes.Name: Div32
nodes.DocComment:
Div32 returns the quotient and remainder of (hi, lo) divided by y:
quo = (hi, lo)/y, rem = (hi, lo)%y with the dividend bits' upper
half in parameter hi and the lower half in parameter lo.
Div32 panics for y == 0 (division by zero) or y <= hi (quotient overflow).

nodes.Name: Div64
nodes.DocComment:
Div64 returns the quotient and remainder of (hi, lo) divided by y:
quo = (hi, lo)/y, rem = (hi, lo)%y with the dividend bits' upper
half in parameter hi and the lower half in parameter lo.
Div64 panics for y == 0 (division by zero) or y <= hi (quotient overflow).

nodes.Name: Rem
nodes.DocComment:
Rem returns the remainder of (hi, lo) divided by y. Rem panics for
y == 0 (division by zero) but, unlike Div, it doesn't panic on a
quotient overflow.

nodes.Name: Rem32
nodes.DocComment:
Rem32 returns the remainder of (hi, lo) divided by y. Rem32 panics
for y == 0 (division by zero) but, unlike [Div32], it doesn't panic
on a quotient overflow.

nodes.Name: Rem64
nodes.DocComment:
Rem64 returns the remainder of (hi, lo) divided by y. Rem64 panics
for y == 0 (division by zero) but, unlike [Div64], it doesn't panic
on a quotient overflow.
